memory_update.text: CHEF should be tracked as an underfollowed center-of-plate distribution candidate because its filings explicitly mention center-of-the-plate proteins, specialty sourcing, and restaurant customers.

PPC is a cleaner protein-processing candidate than many diversified food companies because it discloses value-added chicken/pork products sold to distributors and foodservice operators, but commodity poultry cycles remain a major confounder.

CALM is a second-order restaurant protein-input candidate rather than a classic center-of-plate meat supplier; include only with explicit tracking of foodservice, prepared foods, egg-product capacity, and avian-flu/cage-free constraints.

Need a later pass for private or cooperative restaurant supply-chain entities such as National DCP, OSI Group, Cargill, Koch Foods, Wayne-Sanderson, and other non-public suppliers that may explain hidden dependencies but are not directly investable as US-listed equities.

summary: Expanded the restaurant protein-sourcing node into a focused two-lane public universe. Reference lane anchors include large diversified protein processors, while the underfollowed lane emphasizes companies whose restaurant exposure may be hidden inside foodservice, prepared protein, center-of-plate distribution, or regulated protein-input categories. The best Layer 1B fits are not necessarily pure restaurant stocks; they are processors or distributors whose value-added products, foodservice channels, supply reliability, or protein availability constraints can affect restaurant margins and menu execution.
